tool_calls.name: ask_debt
tool_calls.arguments: {"question": "Please compare two ways to handle the credit card, keeping the household's approved avalanche preference in mind. Look at putting all unallocated surplus on the credit card to clear it fast, since Mara said she would rather clear the card fast."}

tool_calls.name: ask_savings
tool_calls.arguments: {"question": "Please look at Jun's idea: put ₱4,000 extra a month on the credit card and the rest of the surplus to the emergency fund. Show what that does for the emergency fund and the card."}

{"reply":"You have two solid ways to do it.

Jun’s split keeps the emergency fund moving while still paying the card down much faster than minimums. Mara’s fast-pay option clears the card sooner and cuts the card’s interest more.

What I’d weigh is your trade-off between speed and buffer. Your emergency fund already covers 2.1 months, and your approved debt strategy is avalanche, which points extra debt money to the credit card first. Since Mara said she would rather clear the card fast, the strongest fit is the all-extra-to-card option. If keeping the emergency fund growing right away feels more comfortable, the split option is the balanced choice.
